items.title: 67619_Big Nick Nicholas oral history interview
items.q: Billie Holiday, she used to come in all the time and sit down and Bird, you know, we were friends.

ctx.x: Well, now, your father got some ears then?

He had some big ears, baby, Yeah. He said he was blockin' hats in Times Square in 1919. He saved his money up and he went to the Metropolitan Opera to hear Caruso and, a standee,...he says "Nick, I stood up there for over two hours," and he says, "Caruso sound just like a machine." Haha. So I remember all these things. So that sound was instilled in me then. I wasn't even aware of that, see? It was in me. But then I went all through Caruso, I went through Berno Chaliapin, the Russian, for sound. Anybody that had…
Mabel Mercer. Mabel Mercer scared me to death.

items.title: 67619_Big Nick Nicholas oral history interview
items.q: And then, of course, Louis. Louis, you know, he was loved throughout the world. His sound. I admired him so much, you know. ... And I admired Billy Holiday, because she seems to transfix people with her soul and her choice of material, you know what I mean.

ctx.x: we started on, but just the other day you said something to the effect that "It was the women that carried us through there for a while." You named Ella and Sarah Vaughan and whatever. You said, "The musicians kind of fell down there for a while."

Well, what the singers were doin', they were singing a song, but they were singing with a jazz...they were singing like they were playin' a horn. That's the way Billy Holiday sang and Ella sang and Sarah. They sing like they playin' a horn. But the were usin' words, you see. But it has a jazz feeling, you know what I mean. But they were singing words. But those singers, they love musicians, you know, Sarah, Ella and Billy and Carmen, they love musicians. And they were truly jazz singers, because they sound like a…
